facts.claim: The year of Everest's first ascent: Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay, of the British expedition led by John Hunt, on 29 May, by the South Col route.

versions.note: Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay, on May 29, 1953.

source.title: Explorersweb: Mount Everest: Everything You Wanted to Know

facts.claim: The time of day Hillary and Tenzing reached the summit, on 29 May 1953.

source.title: Oxford University Press: Hillary and Tenzing climb Mt. Everest

facts.claim: On the summit in 1953, Tenzing, a Buddhist, buried sweets and biscuits in the snow as an offering to the gods; Hillary left a crucifix John Hunt had given him.

versions.note: Tenzing, a Buddhist, made an offering of food for the mountain; Hillary left a crucifix Hunt had given him.
He buried offerings, sweets from his daughter among them, to the Buddhist deities; Hillary buried a crucifix given to him by Hunt.

source.title: The Irish Times: On top of the world (2023)

facts.claim: The most ascents of Everest by one climber: Kami Rita Sherpa of Thame, the latest on 17 May 2026; his first was in 1994.

source.title: Anadolu: Nepali mountaineer Kami Rita Sherpa summits Everest for record 32nd time (2026)

versions.note: Born in Thame; first climbed Everest in 1994.

source.title: Everest Chronicle: Kami Rita Sherpa scales Everest for record 32nd time (2026)

facts.claim: The most ascents of Everest by a woman: Lhakpa Sherpa, the latest on 17 May 2026.

source.title: Guinness World Records: Most ascents of Everest (female)
The Kathmandu Post: Lhakpa Sherpa scales Everest for record 11th time (2026)

facts.claim: The longest stay on Everest's summit: Babu Chhiri Sherpa, without bottled oxygen, in May 1999.

source.title: Guinness World Records: Longest stay on Everest summit

versions.note: Overnight on the summit without bottled oxygen in May 1999.

source.title: American Alpine Journal: Everest, the Death of Babu Chiri (2002)
